name: Kruskal–Wallis independent-group rank test
definition: Pool N observations and assign midranks. For group i with size n_i and rank total R_i, H=[12Σ_i(R_i²/n_i)/(N(N+1))−3(N+1)]/C, where C=1−Σ_j(t_j³−t_j)/(N³−N). Compare H to χ² with g−1 degrees of freedom.
variables: g groups, t_j sizes of pooled tie blocks, C tie correction
assumptions: Independent samples, exchangeability under the common-distribution null, C>0, and sufficiently large groups for chi-square calibration
limitations: A rejection can reflect unequal distribution shapes, and small groups can require permutation calibration
failure_conditions: A rejection can reflect unequal distribution shapes, and small groups can require permutation calibration

source.citation: SciPy maintainers’ reference and implementation, scipy.stats.kruskal. https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.kruskal.html

name: Friedman complete-block rank test
definition: Rank g methods within each of b complete blocks using midranks. With rank totals R_i, Q=[12Σ_i R_i²/(bg(g+1))−3b(g+1)]/C, where C=1−Σ_jΣ_k(t_jk³−t_jk)/(b(g³−g)). Use an approximate χ²_(g−1) tail.
variables: t_jk size of tie block k within observational block j, C tie correction
assumptions: Blocks are independent, all methods appear in each block, and ranks are exchangeable under the null; C>0
limitations: The chi-square approximation can be inaccurate with small b or g
failure_conditions: The chi-square approximation can be inaccurate with small b or g

source.citation: SciPy maintainers’ reference and implementation, scipy.stats.friedmanchisquare. https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.friedmanchisquare.html

name: Fligner–Killeen scale test
definition: Center each group at its sample median and pool absolute deviations. Let r_j be the pooled midrank and a_j=Φ⁻¹(1/2+r_j/[2(N+1)]). Form Q=Σ_i n_i(ā_i−ā)²/s_a² with pooled sample variance s_a²; use χ²_(g−1) as a large-sample reference.
variables: N pooled size, n_i group size, ā_i group score mean, ā pooled score mean, Φ normal CDF
assumptions: Independent groups, positive score variance, and common distribution shape for a pure scale interpretation
limitations: Different shapes can affect the statistic even when a chosen scale summary agrees
failure_conditions: Different shapes can affect the statistic even when a chosen scale summary agrees

source.citation: SciPy maintainers’ reference and implementation, scipy.stats.fligner. https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.fligner.html

name: Ansari–Bradley two-sample scale test
definition: Rank pooled observations from the outermost values toward the center using scores c(r)=min(r,N+1−r) for ordered positions r. Average these scores within any tied block. A=Σ_(observations in sample 1)c is compared to its fixed-group-size exchangeable distribution, or a tie-adjusted large-sample approximation.
variables: N pooled size, r position in sorted sample, c center-weighted score, A observed statistic
assumptions: Independent samples with equal location under the scale comparison; shared continuous shape for scale interpretation
limitations: Location differences affect ranks, and standard no-tie exact calibration fails in tied samples
failure_conditions: Location differences affect ranks, and standard no-tie exact calibration fails in tied samples
computation: O(N log N) to build scores; reference-distribution cost depends on calibration
